title: kith-tui: read-receipt feedback loop duplicates messages
description:
Rehearsal1 (kith 062df2c, chinwag 947b098, 3 users). One message from alice rendered 21+ times (full pane) on bob and carol within 125 ms and kept growing; each client hot-loops ~290 req/s, chinwag at 64% CPU with 2 looping clients, bob's Message state 1250 -> 3434 -> 6174 in ~1 min while the server stores exactly 1 message.

Cause (event.rs handle_state_change, Message arm): ids in Message/changes 'updated' are pushed to state.messages as NEW lines with no check against state.message_ids, then send_read_receipts sets readAt (fresh timestamp each time) on them -> real Message state change -> SSE StateChange -> Message/changes reports the same id as updated -> append + receipt again. Never terminates.

Knock-on effects seen: Chat StateChanges wait behind the Message backlog (new direct chat appeared 10-20+ s late; unread badge stayed '(1)' after server cleared it to 0); user's own sent message did not appear in their own pane; during a 3 s server restart each client logged ~600 failed Message/changes.

Spec: RFC 8620 s5.2 'updated: ids for records that have been updated' -> client must replace the existing entry, not append. draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 'Marking as Read': readAt is an update; a client should only set it when it is null. Fix: dedupe updated ids against message_ids (replace in place), and only send receipts for messages whose readAt is null.

Evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mark-PROJECT-chinwag/d56f3967-d390-456c-a3d8-9501efe458da/scratchpad/rehearsal1/shots/03-*-alice-msg.txt, 04-*-replies.txt, json/st-bob.resp.json, logs/chinwag1.log (request rate).
close_reason: Message/changes updated ids replace in place, destroyed removed; receipts only for readAt-unset inbound; ReadPosition only on append. Tests: handle_state_change_updated_id_replaces_existing_line, handle_state_change_destroyed_id_removes_line, handle_state_change_already_read_update_sends_no_write, receipt_loop_settles_when_server_bumps_state_on_write
